method: Independent static second review using atomscan, cleave facts and decoded strings, binwalk, rizin control-flow/call-site analysis, and Go nm/objdump. No sample was executed. No external scanner, feed or advisory was used as verdict evidence.
beacon_evidence: File 8a370f... is an x86 DLL despite its .exe suffix. DOS-header machine code computes the raw ReflectiveLoader address at 0x8079, calls it, then invokes the returned entry with reason 4. _ReflectiveLoader@4 maps a native image, walks PEB module/export lists with ROR13 hashing, allocates executable memory, resolves imports and performs relocation/entry transfer.

Preferred VA 0x10008c21 handles custom reason 4 by calling 0x10009619 and then the task loop at 0x100015c4. At 0x10009643 it XORs all 4096 bytes of the settings table at VA 0x10031028/raw 0x2f228 with 0x69; code from 0x10009660 parses typed setting records.

The independently decoded table contains DNS mode=1, port=443, sleep=5000ms, an RSA public key, ns7/ns8/ns9.softline.top hosts, GET/POST methods and HTTP transformations impersonating Amazon headers/paths. It also contains x86/x64 rundll32 spawn paths and a named-pipe template. These are configured values, not observed connections.

The loop calls DNS command/control paths, examines a network-order control word against 0xfffffff0 at 0x10001858 and selects fetch operations at 0x100018bf/0x100018cd. Query helpers 0x1000357b and 0x1000361b issue DnsQuery_A at 0x10003598/0x10003636 with TXT/AAAA query types, retry on failure and process returned data. This verifies tasking implementation beyond hostname templates.

Injection helper 0x10005721 links VirtualAllocEx -> WriteProcessMemory (0x10005785) -> VirtualProtectEx(PAGE_EXECUTE_READ). Caller 0x10005859 receives that allocation and passes allocation+entry offset to CreateRemoteThread at 0x1000593d using the same process handle. The self-PID alternative uses a local allocator and CreateThread. Caller 0x1000597f checks target architecture and reaches the injection helper at 0x10005a16.

The nonmapped tail is largely alphabetic padding/filename material. Decoded string leads were inspected; the settings decode is corroborated by its live initialization routine. No additional payload behavior is inferred from random or mechanically decoded text.
go_evidence: Go main.main is at 0x58ed20. checkForAdmin at 0x58ecd0 attempts to open PHYSICALDRIVE0; this is an access test, not destructive disk I/O. Failure builds Start-Process -FilePath <argv[0]> -Verb runAs and calls powershell.exe via exec.Command/Start at 0x58f1c3/0x58f1cf. This requests consent; it does not bypass UAC.

The admin branch checks TEMP/GData.txt, exits if present, otherwise waits 20 seconds and creates the marker. It calls GetArchive at 0x58eeb0 with a TEMP ZIP destination and an S3 ZIP URL. GetArchive at 0x58f220 calls os.Create, net/http.Get and io.Copy with the response body and output file.

Extract at 0x58f3b0 opens the ZIP, opens members, joins destination/member paths, checks the cleaned destination prefix, makes directories and copies bytes to created files. main uses C:/G DATA Security Software/ as destination, removes the downloaded ZIP, waits, and starts AVK.exe at 0x58f0d3/0x58f0df. Those chosen names do not establish hostile behavior on their own.

The Go executable appends the ENTIRE supplied 351213-byte Beacon file at offset 0x4bc201. Direct byte comparison equals the whole 8a370f... sample, including its tail, and its SHA256 is the queued 8a370f... hash. Atomscan separately analyzes the mapped embedded PE as child unit 1.

The encoded-PowerShell template is at parent raw 0x4e7afd inside that embedded DLL, corresponding to 8a raw 0x2b8fc. It is not used by the traced Go main, whose only PowerShell use is the unencoded consent request. No path from the Go entry point to activation of the appended Beacon was established.
judgment: Both MALICIOUS: the executable reflective bootstrap, configured covert tasking and remote execution implementation establish an implant rather than inert indicators. The Go carrier contains that exact complete implant. Its download/install and consent request remain neutral capabilities. Cobalt Strike can be used in authorized testing, but no engagement authorization, disclosure or deployment context was supplied. Do not assume registry provenance establishes either trust or malice.

corrections.action: Remove unsupported composite; retain every constituent observation.
corrections.reason: Four same-file references do not bind a downloaded ZIP to an encoded-PowerShell launch. The real Go program disproves the claimed relationship: its PowerShell template is inside an appended implant. An inert return-only PE containing the same independent strings also fires the old composite. This corrects unsupported flow/intent, not a technique justified by a synthetic near miss alone. The precise Go download/certutil/script-launch objective is preserved and checked against the existing external-to-batch hostile fixture.

corrections.action: Move to host-profile discovery, add token/module-name boundaries and case-insensitivity. Move the existing shell invocation atom alongside it without changing that matcher.
corrections.reason: The Go runtime type runtime.systeminfo is not the Windows command. Substring matching also hit systeminformation, while missing SYSTEMINFO.EXE. All exact objective references were updated; ordinary systeminfo paths, command arguments and Python popen discovery remain covered.

corrections.action: Name the reference evidence honestly and require it within 256 bytes. Update the DCSync consumer.
corrections.reason: The Go TLS aesKey type is at raw 0x1926eb; Kerberos references are at 0x4e7949 in the appended DLL. Their distant coincidence is not an authentication option. The nearby-reference observation and hostile DCSync-key-auth consumer both retain positive controls; standalone AES key and Kerberos references remain untouched.

corrections.action: Relocate to package-reference metadata, raise to notable and require package/symbol raw-byte token boundaries. Update the Telegram-archive consumer.
corrections.reason: A complete standard-package reference is import metadata, not ZIP creation/extraction and not universal baseline behavior. Removing the false composite exposed a presentation-strip loss of the previously referenced baseline atom; the relocated notable finding preserves the supported observation. No ZIP writer/reader capability rule was removed. Validation exposed a further old overmatch in an existing do-nothing Go ELF: the GODEBUG catalog concatenates crypto/x509archive/zipskip_headers despite no ZIP import in the fixture source. Requiring package/symbol boundaries excludes that catalog, while preserving archive/zip and archive/zip.OpenReader observations. This is a matcher correction, not a severity demotion or filename exemption.

corrections.action: Include PE/DLL command text; keep notable and describe the option text.
corrections.reason: The compiled Go program constructs -Verb runAs, but the atom was scoped only to selected source types. This captures the actual consent request without an escalation-abuse claim. Existing positive source scope and regex remain unchanged.

consumer_audit.go_chain: No exact YAML consumers and no payload/file-exec ancestor selector consuming the retired composite were found.
consumer_audit.systeminfo: All exact consuming YAML references were updated. No direct process/profile directory selectors were found. The three broader sysinfo selectors (two endpoint exceptions and a Perl exfiltration rule) retain utility observations under the same ancestor. The corrected exclusions are intended only for non-command tokens.
consumer_audit.archive_reference: The Telegram archive-exfil composite is the sole remaining exact consumer; it now explicitly names the metadata observation. No archive/zip or builtin ancestor selector consumers were found.
consumer_audit.kerberos: The DCSync key-auth composite is the sole exact consumer. Positive near-key context and the hostile DCSync conjunction pass. No auth/session ancestor selectors were found.
consumer_audit.runas: Exact consumers reviewed in PowerShell arguments, installer, prompt escalation, RMM provisioning and install-hook rules. Most retain source-type gates; no generic elevation ancestor selectors were found. Rescans show no unintended new composite on either supplied sample.

coverage: Every hostile Beacon finding and the ROR13 resolver detection remains unchanged on the standalone DLL and embedded child. Three independent family signatures cover DNS tasking, reflective mapping and XOR settings; no duplicate hostile rule was added for score or count. The Go-only hostile flow claim is intentionally lost. Systeminfo and AES/Kerberos false associations disappear; ZIP reference identity is preserved at its correct location. There is no classifier disagreement: both remain probability 0.995.

validation.checks: 19 focused after-controls include retained hostile Go stage and DCSync consumer, SYSINFO positives and runtime near misses, bounded Kerberos references, UAC option text, and preserved ZIP/exec/encoded-command atoms. Before-controls record the original false matches. Final make validate is run after reports, scans and markers. The two added controls cover concatenated GODEBUG catalog text and the existing do-nothing Go ELF itself. First validation failed on this reference matcher in eight copies/wrappers of that ELF; token boundaries correct the demonstrated non-import match. Extracted Go string-table slices conceal that neighboring catalog text, so the final matcher uses raw-byte token boundaries; all 19 controls pass.
validation.engine_caveat: Atomscan reports feature-spec v18 versus extractor v19 and zeros newer features. The before/after model and observed verdict nevertheless agree; no YAML workaround or score inflation was applied.
validation.final_scan_confirmation: After the raw-byte matcher correction, atomscan on both samples still yields identical finding ID sets to scan-comparison.json, including the embedded PE child; both probabilities remain 0.995.
